findings.message: This is an instance fix. Last round's finding said the gap covers every tool whose service picks a stricter permission per step, but `step` was added only to fi2. hr1 has the same gap. The card shows HR approving Sophie Nguyen's leave as HR, not as her manager. `chainFor` in modules/leave/server/scope.ts:36 grants that HR step only through `leave:admin`. `approve_leave` declares `leave:approve`, and PM, Engineer, Finance, Sales, Payroll and Leadership all hold that through MANAGE (modules/leave/module.ts:10, 27-32). So the hr1 row only proves that some role holds `leave:approve`. It says nothing about HR's step. The cause is that `step` is optional and nothing makes a card set it, so any new card on a step-dependent tool passes silently. Fix: set `step: "leave:admin"` on hr1. Then either derive the step permission from the tool's service, or keep a list of tools with step-dependent services (approve_expense, reject_expense, approve_leave and the other leave decide tools) and fail any card on those tools that has no `step`. Also add a rejecting row per step, e.g. Engineer at the HR step of approve_leave.
findings.scenario: Remove `leave:admin` from HR's grants in modules/leave/module.ts. HR can no longer approve a non-report's leave, so hr1's 'Approve leave' claim is false. The test `HR card hr1 runs approve_leave` still passes, because `canEver(HR, "leave:approve")` is true through MANAGE, or would be for any role given MANAGE.

findings.message: The new rejection test calls `holds("Engineer", "expenses:approve-finance")` directly and never goes through the card check that the fix added. It doesn't prove the fix works: delete `...(step ? [step] : [])` from the loop at line 25 and every test stays green. It also has only one row, where B2 asks for the named case plus two others. Fix: pull the per-card check into a function, such as `check(role, card)`, that both the passing rows and a rejecting table use. Feed it at least three cards whose tool permission the role holds but whose step it doesn't: Engineer on `{ tool: "approve_expense", step: "expenses:approve-finance" }`, PM on `{ tool: "approve_leave", step: "leave:admin" }`, and a third such as HR on the same expense step. Expect each one to be rejected.
findings.scenario: Change line 25 to `for (const p of [permission!])`, which ignores `step`. fi2 still passes, and `rejects a step the role cannot take` still passes, so the suite goes green with the fix removed.
